label: Khawagi G010: antipsychotic in dementia at age 65 or older without psychosis at supply
title: Antipsychotic in dementia at age 65 or older without psychosis at supply
statement: (N) Patient aged ≥65 with dementia but no psychosis - is prescribed an antipsychotic

source.document: Quality and safety of medication use in primary care: consensus validation of a new set of explicit medication assessment criteria and prioritisation of topics for improvement
source.citation: Dreischulte T, Grant AM, McCowan C, McAnaw JJ, Guthrie B. BMC Clinical Pharmacology 2012;12:5.
source.credit: © 2012 Dreischulte et al., licensee BioMed Central Ltd. Table 5. DOI 10.1186/1472-6904-12-5. CC BY 2.0. Local selection and record conventions added.
source.modification_notice: The published statement is reproduced with local screening and case rules added.

plain_summary: At age 65 or older, even a short antipsychotic supply warrants review if dementia is recorded and the record excludes psychosis at supply. Australian guidance differs: oral risperidone is approved for up to 12 weeks for persistent agitation or aggression in moderate to severe Alzheimer dementia when non-drug measures have failed (Risperdal product information, 2026).

medicine_groups.name: Antipsychotics
medicine_groups.note: Oral and injectable antipsychotics count. Check the reason for supply, including non-psychiatric uses. Flupentixol decanoate is the depot form of flupentixol. Count the exposure once.

needs_facts.meets: The record or the pharmacist confirms that dementia had been diagnosed by the reviewed supply date. If timing is unclear, leave it open.

options.words: Dementia had been diagnosed by this supply
No dementia diagnosis by this supply

needs_facts.meets: A dated assessment or the pharmacist confirms status at this supply. Review if neither current psychosis nor a continuing psychotic illness was present. A resolved episode alone does not exclude review. An ongoing illness such as schizophrenia in remission does. Unknown status leaves the finding open.

options.words: No current psychosis and no continuing psychotic illness at this supply
Current psychosis or a continuing psychotic illness at this supply

rule_for_models: Use age at supply. Give no finding below age 65. If age is unknown and the other evidence fits, report only a possible finding and ask whether the patient was at least 65. At age 65 or older, cite the Group A antipsychotic supply of any duration, the evidence of dementia by that date and the evidence that neither psychosis nor a continuing psychotic illness was present at supply. A pharmacist answer about this supply can establish either fact. Give no finding if dementia had not been diagnosed by this supply or current psychosis or a continuing psychotic illness is documented. A non-psychiatric indication, such as nausea, does not exclude a listed antipsychotic or establish that psychosis is absent. Record the reason if known. If dementia or psychosis status is missing or uncertain and the other evidence fits, report only a possible finding. Cite available lines and name each missing fact. Ask the patient or carer whether dementia has been diagnosed, why the medicine was prescribed and whether a psychotic illness has been recorded.
cannot_be_seen: A silent record cannot establish psychosis status at supply. Supply alone cannot establish the indication, symptoms or benefit.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm the dementia diagnosis and psychosis status at supply and review the indication and intended duration of this antipsychotic?
